questions.q: What separates responsible resilience from unconditional perseverance?
choices: Persistence always reflects strength of character.
Its value depends on conditions and the usefulness of the goal.
It should replace formal assessment.
It matters only after a setback has ended.
questions.explanation: The second paragraph judges effort partly by the likelihood of meaningful change under actual conditions.

questions.q: What problem arises when resilience becomes a moral requirement?
choices: Improvement becomes impossible to measure.
Students may be encouraged to rest too often.
Schools must remove all individual responsibilities.
Structural barriers can be mistaken for personal shortcomings.
questions.explanation: The opening warns that a moral demand to bounce back can obscure the sources of an individual's setback.

questions.q: What limitation is illustrated by measuring rapid score improvements?
choices: Practising familiar material is never useful.
Deeper learning always produces quick marks.
A real gain can conceal other valuable forms of learning.
Exploration cannot be compared with any form of practice.
questions.explanation: The assessment comparison shows that score gains measure a narrower outcome than intellectual development.

questions.q: Why contrast endurance with actually benefiting from education?
choices: To show that visible effort may coexist with poor educational support.
To argue that long-term effort should not be rewarded.
To suggest that persistence is a substitute for teaching.
To make personal effort irrelevant to schooling.
questions.explanation: The author contrasts enduring obstacles with receiving the resources needed to learn.

questions.q: What does it mean for an indicator to 'colonise' an activity?
choices: It becomes legally compulsory in every school.
It starts to dominate the activity it was meant to describe.
It makes all numerical measurements false.
It prevents students from achieving higher scores.
questions.explanation: The metaphor in paragraph three implies that measurement takes over the activity it once merely described.

questions.q: Why does the conclusion reject the claim that talent is fixed?
choices: To suggest abilities are completely inherited.
To replace perseverance with rest as the only goal.
To reject assessment as an educational tool.
To avoid turning criticism of compulsory perseverance into fatalism.
questions.explanation: The conclusion rejects fixed talent and powerlessness even as it criticises compulsory optimism.

questions.q: How should a school respond to pupils overcoming persistent resource shortages?
choices: Reward more hours of visible effort.
Advise every pupil to develop more resilience.
Examine and address the obstacles that require extraordinary endurance.
Remove all targets for students receiving support.
questions.explanation: Celebrating effort can allow institutions to avoid asking why an obstacle persists.

questions.q: How might abandoning a poor goal demonstrate maturity?
choices: It can reveal judgement about whether further persistence serves a purpose.
It shows the learner has no interest in improvement.
It demonstrates that goals need not be evaluated.
It proves the original goal was always impossible.
questions.explanation: The third paragraph sees the capacity to reconsider an unsuitable goal as mature judgement.

questions.q: Which policy is most compatible with the author's conclusion?
choices: Compulsory public rankings of weekly improvement.
Providing support while allowing learners to reconsider their aims.
Treating every private activity as a performance target.
Replacing all personal choices with standard plans.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph combines support to continue with the freedom to reconsider goals.

questions.q: What should we infer about an accurate but narrow assessment indicator?
choices: It must be discarded as an entirely false description.
It shows slow learners are less determined.
It explains everything that education should value.
It may describe something real while omitting other essential outcomes.
questions.explanation: The author says an indicator need not be false to answer a much narrower question.
